title: Ishan Kishan Closes In on Three Major T20 Records Against New Zealand
excerpt: The wicketkeeper-batter needs seven runs to break Suryakumar Yadav's Indian calendar-year record, 139 to pass Mohammad Rizwan's Test-nation mark, and 46 to reach 2,000 career T20I runs as the five-match series opens in Christchurch.
body:
• Ishan Kishan needs seven runs to pass Suryakumar Yadav's record of 1,164 T20I runs by an Indian in a calendar year, set in 2022.
  • Kishan has scored 1,158 runs in 34 T20I innings this year at an average of 37.35 and a strike rate of 172.06, with one century and seven half-centuries.
  • He is 139 runs short of Mohammad Rizwan's 1,326 runs in 2021, the calendar-year T20I record for a batter from a Test-playing nation, and 46 runs short of 2,000 career T20I runs.
  • India's five-match T20I series against New Zealand starts in Christchurch on Thursday, followed by a three-match series against Sri Lanka in December.

Kishan opens the New Zealand series chasing records

Wicketkeeper-batter Ishan Kishan goes into India's five-match T20I series against New Zealand, starting in Christchurch on Thursday, with three calendar-year records in reach. Kishan has scored 1,158 T20I runs in 34 innings this year and needs seven more to pass the Indian record of 1,164 set by Suryakumar Yadav in 2022, according to the figures reported by The Times of India via eDailyGraph. His runs this year have come at an average of 37.35 and a strike rate of 172.06, including a century and seven half-centuries, in what the reports describe as a breakthrough year batting at number three.

The three marks in sight

The second record is the biggest one. Pakistan's Mohammad Rizwan scored 1,326 T20I runs in 2021, the most in a calendar year by a batter from a Test-playing nation. Kishan is 139 runs short of that mark with five matches against New Zealand and a three-match series against Sri Lanka in December still to play this year. The third milestone is a career landmark rather than a calendar one: Kishan has 1,954 runs in 66 T20Is at an average of 31.51 and a strike rate of 148.81, with one century and 13 half-centuries and a highest score of 103. He needs 46 runs to become the seventh Indian to reach 2,000 T20I runs, as detailed by GyanhiGyan.

A fourth figure sits behind the headline three. Across all T20 cricket this year, Kishan has scored 1,760 runs in 49 matches at an average of 38.26 and a strike rate above 175. He needs 240 more to become the first Indian to score 2,000 T20 runs in a calendar year. Only two batters have done it before: West Indies' Nicholas Pooran, with 2,331 runs in 2024, and Rizwan, with 2,036 in 2021.

Why the numbers matter

Calendar-year records are a measure of volume as much as form: they require a player to hold his place through a full schedule and keep scoring at a high strike rate while doing so. Kishan's 172.06 strike rate this year is well above his career T20I strike rate of 148.81, which is why the record chase is realistic across eight remaining internationals rather than a mathematical long shot. The Indian squad for the series, as listed in the reports, includes Shreyas Iyer as captain, with Kishan and Sanju Samson as the wicketkeeper-batters.

For diaspora fans following the series from the US, the record watch gives each of the five matches in New Zealand a running thread: the Indian calendar-year record could fall in the first game, while the Rizwan mark will likely be decided across the full series and the Sri Lanka matches in December.

What's next

The series opens in Christchurch on Thursday and runs over five matches. Kishan needs one scoring innings to take the Indian record; the Test-nation record and the 2,000-run T20 year depend on his aggregate across the New Zealand and Sri Lanka series before the calendar turns.
